# OVERRIDES.tsv - labels you decide by hand (used by triage_evidence_v2.py)
# HOW TO USE: one game = one copy of this file. Copy it, rename it to OVERRIDES.tsv, put it in that game's folder.
# Lines that do not start with an 8-digit hex address are ignored (comments are safe).
# ENTRY = function address, 8 hex digits, no 0x.   LABEL = KEEP | WRAP | REPLACE | UNKNOWN.   NOTE = free text.
# KEEP = game code with its own logic | WRAP = same interface, new body for OS calls | REPLACE = compiler/OS provides it
# WHY USE IT
# - Triage is a guess from names, imports, strings and call links. Your label wins over every rule.
# - Fix a wrong guess, and settle the functions that are left as UNKNOWN.
# - Helpers follow you: a small function called ONLY by a function you labeled gets the same label,
#   so you do not have to list them one by one.
# - It survives every re-run. Triage overwrites its own files each time, but never this one.
# - Your NOTE is saved in FUNCTIONS.tsv (REASON column), so you remember why.
# WHEN TO USE
# - After the first run: open QUEUE_UNKNOWN.tsv, look at each function in LITE_AC, add a line, run again.
# - When a label in FUNCTIONS.tsv looks wrong to you (a launcher marked REPLACE, a runtime helper marked KEEP).
# - When you know something the script cannot see (what a function does from reading it).
# WHEN NOT TO USE
# - When the guess is already right. Do not label everything by hand, it is slow and the script is good at the easy ones.
# - For a whole C runtime zone: set --crt-start in the command instead of listing every function here.
# - With a file from another game. Addresses belong to ONE exe. A copy from another game gives wrong labels.
# - In the scripts folder. Keep it in that game's folder, or it would apply to every game.
# - To hide a problem. If many labels are wrong, check the grouping or the settings first.
# HOW EACH LABEL AFFECTS TRIAGE (check it in FUNCTIONS.tsv and the QUEUE files after the run)
# KEEP    the function is KEEP and goes into QUEUE_KEEP.tsv, so the LLM converts it.
#         Helpers called only by it become KEEP (WRAP if they call Windows APIs).
# WRAP    the function is WRAP and goes into QUEUE_WRAP.tsv: keep its signature, write a new body.
#         Helpers called only by it become KEEP (WRAP if they call Windows APIs).
# REPLACE the function leaves the conversion queues, nothing is converted.
#         Helpers called only by it become REPLACE (UNKNOWN if they have their own game strings).
# UNKNOWN the function stays in QUEUE_UNKNOWN.tsv until you decide. It is a note to yourself.
